name: Cavern Club
description: A cellar club on Mathew Street where the Beatles played hundreds of times in the early 1960s. Today’s club is a rebuild on part of the original site.

name: St George’s Hall
description: A huge neoclassical hall opposite Lime Street station, opened in 1854 with a concert hall and law courts under one roof.

name: Royal Albert Dock
places: International Slavery Museum, Royal Albert Dock
description: Brick and iron dock warehouses opened in 1846, now home to museums, including the International Slavery Museum, and shops and cafés.

name: Anfield
description: Liverpool FC’s stadium, with the Kop stand, a statue of manager Bill Shankly and a memorial to the 97 who died at Hillsborough in 1989.

name: Liverpool Town Hall
description: Liverpool’s 18th-century town hall and Exchange Flags, the square behind it where merchants traded, with a monument to Nelson.

name: Liverpool Cathedral
description: Britain’s largest cathedral, a red sandstone Anglican church built between 1904 and 1978. You can climb the tower.

name: Metropolitan Cathedral
places: Metropolitan Cathedral of Christ the King
description: Liverpool’s Catholic cathedral, a round 1960s church with a stained-glass lantern tower, built over the crypt of a far larger unbuilt design.

name: St Peter’s Church, Woolton
description: A village church in south Liverpool. John Lennon and Paul McCartney first met at its summer fête in 1957.

name: St Luke’s Church
places: St Luke’s bombed-out church, Leece Street
description: A Gothic church gutted by bombs in the 1941 Blitz and left as a roofless shell. It now stands as a war memorial and hosts events.

name: Cunard Building
description: The former head office of the Cunard shipping line, finished in 1917, one of three large Edwardian buildings on the waterfront at Pier Head.

name: Mersey Ferries terminal
description: The Pier Head terminal for the ferries across the River Mersey to the Wirral. River cruises leave from here every day.
